notes: CARRY-FORWARD GATE. metrics_placeholder=true and pass_rate=null mean this baseline is NOT a measurement. Per eval/foxy-everyday/harness/verdict.ts, a run that supplies no live control arm AND falls back to this file is forced INCONCLUSIVE — it can never read as PASS or REGRESS. This mirrors the B1 harness's placeholder gate (eval/rag/baseline/ncert-baseline-v1.json).

HOW TO POPULATE. Run the full 54-case set with ff_foxy_everyday_examples_v1 OFF, capture the responses, judge them with this rubric, and copy the measured pooled pass_rate and harm_count here. That control arm is the number flag-ON must beat by required_margin_over_control. Populating this file is an assessment review, never an auto-refresh: an eval whose baseline updates itself cannot detect a regression.

PREFERRED PRACTICE: run BOTH arms in the same session and pass --off. A same-session control arm is strictly better than this committed baseline, because prompt, model routing and corpus all drift between sessions and a stale control arm silently inflates the margin.

The bars mirrored here are the ones in eval/foxy-everyday/harness/rubric.ts, which is the single source of truth. They are duplicated into this file only so a reviewer reading a committed baseline can see what it was measured against. If the two disagree, rubric.ts wins and this file is stale.

Changing rubric_version INVALIDATES this baseline: verdict.ts forces INCONCLUSIVE when the run's rubric version differs from the baseline's, because scores produced under different anchors are not comparable.
